name: 1-Testosterone (1-Test / dihydroboldenone)

card.summary: A DHT-derived designer steroid once sold online as a supplement; controlled in the US since 2005 and untested in human trials.
card.note: Controlled substance in the US; animal data only.

quick.overview:
1-Testosterone is a synthetic androgen sold in the past as a muscle-building prohormone.

Only animal data and doping-detection literature are described; no human trials were found.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor selectively, and an animal study reported potency comparable to testosterone propionate in androgen-sensitive tissues.
quick.risks: In the animal study it also increased liver weight. It has been a US Schedule III substance since 2005.

lead: 1-Testosterone (1-Test, 1-T, dihydroboldenone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid that was sold online as a muscle-building supplement. People who used it, and the marketers who sold it, were after the same outcome as with other androgens: more lean mass and a fuller, more muscular physique.[1]

Chemically it is a 5-alpha-reduced derivative of boldenone and a relative of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), differing from testosterone by a double bond at the 1(2) position instead of the 4(5) position.[1] A 2006 animal study described in Wikipedia reported strong androgen-receptor binding and growth of androgen-sensitive muscle at doses comparable to testosterone propionate.[1]

It was legally sold in the United States until 2005, when it became a Schedule III controlled substance.[1] Wikipedia lists no brand names and no human clinical data for the compound.[1] Designer and prohormone steroids as a category generally have little toxicology or pharmacology research behind them.[2]

chain: Androgen-sensitive muscle tissue grows in animal tests
Users sought more lean mass and a fuller physique
angle.text: 1-Testosterone was marketed to people wanting to build muscle. The only published pharmacology is an animal study in which it grew the levator ani muscle about as much as testosterone propionate did.

paras: 1-Testosterone is a derivative of dihydrotestosterone with a double bond between carbons 1 and 2 in the A ring. It is also described as the 5-alpha-reduced form of boldenone.[1] Related prohormone forms include 1-androstenediol and 1-androstenedione, and the latter can be made from stanolone acetate.[1]

A 2006 animal study reported high androgenic and anabolic potency without prior metabolism, with highly selective androgen-receptor binding and strong receptor-dependent transactivation.[1] At equimolar doses it matched testosterone propionate in growing the prostate, seminal vesicles and levator ani muscle. Unlike testosterone propionate, it also increased liver weight.[1]
No studies found. The animal work above is the main published pharmacology.[1]

The compound was sold legally online in the United States until 2005, when it was reclassified as a Schedule III drug.[1] Many countries lack general analogue laws, so slightly modified steroid structures have at times fallen outside existing bans, while others such as Australia regulate by chemical structure.[2]
Doping use can be detected in urine by gas chromatography, according to a 2005 case study cited by Wikipedia.[1]

timeline.event: Reclassified as a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States after being sold legally online.[1]
An animal study reports androgen-receptor potency comparable to testosterone propionate.[1]
